Run from the repository root: python -I -X utf8 dag/pfp/campaign/make_queue.py

Write the derivation-campaign queue: unattempted OPEN/CONDITIONAL/IMPORTED nodes with a mathematical statement, ranked by
downstream impact (trunk weighted x3). Coordination/custody records are excluded by stage and by statement shape.

queue.statement: Five open bridge obligations (register rows GEN-WDP-O01..O05): O01 carrier/signature/law/challenge-generation floor; O02 source transition/admission systems to the WDP bridge by preservation/reflection maps; O03 dynamic carrier transport and higher fillers; O04 effect/probability, scalar and Hilbert choices; O05 governance refinement.
queue.bottleneck: O01..O05 remain open in the register. PregenesisWdpBridgeObligations records the symmetrised-adjacency candidate only: it is not a directed-step certificate, while the identity on adjacency is one, so O02 is not refuted. The integer relation p * p = 2 * q * q has no positive solution and is not the O04 scalar or Hilbert choice. No source admission system is given a preservation map. Checked slice, status unchanged. Narrowed finite case, status left OPEN: on any finite window, symmetrised adjacency is false at a pair exactly when both directed adjacencies are false; on two vertices that symmetrisation is not a directed-step certificate, since edge01 and edge10 differ as directed steps and both have pair-defect true at (0,1); the identity on adjacency is a directed-step certificate on every finite window; and no positive integers p, q satisfy p * p = 2 * q * q, with the numerical case 1 * 1 = 1 and 2 * 1 * 1 = 2. O01, O03, O04, O05, and the existence of an O02 map from a source admission system stay open.

queue.statement: Sectors are residual sectors with declared finite nonnegative masses mu(s), total M > 0. The carrier is the weight vector w. No derivation of w from the Phi1 / Gamma2 residual is given in the sources read: w is an input to QM_003, QM_012 and QM_020.
queue.bottleneck: The general n-cycle, the weighted L1 form with declared masses, the sum-of-squares reading of Gamma2, and any selector other than these two length-4 holonomy checks stay open. The pairs (2, 0) and (0, 2) are one witness that a common coordinate sum does not fix the pair.

queue.statement: The pass from L1 weights to a finite Hilbert carrier imports structure the finite papers do not derive: a square-root field, a complex field, U(1) phases, an inner product, orthogonal additivity, Haar-independent phases, and linear isometric dynamics. QM_020 states that it does not derive quantum mechanics. QM_122 recovers matrices over the Gaussian integers and leaves ordinary matrix algebras over the complex numbers unrecovered. Python, Rust, and Lean 4 must name each import and keep it imported. A finite matrix calculation is not a discharge of the import list.
queue.bottleneck: List each imported structure the finite Hilbert lift still requires, and do not discharge them by naming quantum mechanics. Checked slice, status unchanged. Narrowed in Lean 4 and an independent Python verifier to three exact finite/algebraic components and non-discharge fences: (1) Gaussian-integer 2x2 matrix algebra recovery (QM_122 Pauli involutions and commutator sigmaX * sigmaY = i * sigmaZ, norm multiplicativity) and QM_122 / QM_020 C_4 cochain syndromes (gauss_int_norm_multiplicative, qm122_pauli_gaussian_integer_commutators_and_squares, qm122_and_qm020_cochain_syndrome_and_shadow_replay); (2) non-recovery of the square-root field ((2p + 1)^2 != 2q^2), complex division (unnormalized Hadamard squares to 2 * sigmaI != sigmaI with 2 * sigmaI non-invertible in M_2(Z[i])), and continuous U(1) phases (only 4 units in Z[i] vs. Pythagorean (3/5, 4/5) in Q[i]) (import_fence_sqrt_two_parity_obstruction, import_fence_gaussian_integers_not_a_field_hadamard_unnormalized, import_fence_gaussian_units_vs_u1_phases); and (3) L1 norm violation of the Jordan-von Neumann parallelogram law (8 != 4), orthogonal-additivity cross-term and sign-phase averaging, L1 stochastic vs. L2 isometric norm contraction, and the 7-field HilbertLiftImportLedger truth-table fence (import_fence_l1_norm_fails_parallelogram_law, import_fence_orthogonal_additivity_and_phase_averaging, import_fence_l1_stochastic_not_l2_isometry, seven_hilbert_lift_imports_audit_fence).

queue.statement: Transitive sector symmetry of the quadratic readout: relabelling sectors by any permutation in a set whose generated group acts transitively does not change the readout. This is the second law under which the inner product is selected up to scale; it is supplied, not derived from primitive difference, and sectors with distinguished labels would break it (then the diagonal is constant only on orbits).
queue.bottleneck: No finite-theory primitive forces readout invariance under sector relabelling; H006 supplies the permutation envelope only. Deriving the law, or recording which sector labels are distinguished, is item 1 of the run next steps. The campaign module L1SectorSymmetry does not weaken the law: it takes invariance under a permutation set S as a hypothesis and shows that a symmetric, sector-additive readout has a diagonal that is constant on each orbit of the group generated by S (diag_const_on_orbit), with diag(1,2) on two sectors and diag(1,1,2) on three sectors as countermodels to a scalar form when S is not transitive. Transitivity of S is still the supplied law.
imported_structure: transitive sector symmetry of the readout: assumption

queue.statement: U(1) phases (unit complex numbers) act on sector amplitudes. QM_122 shows a sign carrier suffices for some finite tasks and that excluding it needs an extra non-exponent-two condition. The selector for C / U(1) belongs to QM_028 / QM_062 (another segment).
queue.bottleneck: See L1-U1-SELECTOR-OTHER-SEGMENT.

queue.statement: Hilbert tensor product as the unique way to combine systems. On Bool x Bool a bilinear integer-homogeneous Kronecker-normalized map equals the pointwise product; a weaker same-host combining interface has a rival (dump-the-right-report map).
queue.bottleneck: The Hilbert-space tensor product is not derived as the unique way to combine systems. The agreement above uses additivity, integer homogeneity and the identity tag (i, j) on one Bool-by-Bool host. The dump-right map is a same-host rival whose tag collapses the second Boolean factor, so a weaker tag does not select the pointwise product. A second presented carrier and a physical composition rule stay imported (QM_122 7.1 item 1).

queue.bottleneck: The class of completely positive trace-preserving maps on a Hilbert space is not derived. Choi positivity, Kraus form and a Stinespring realization of that class stay imported. The Boolean collapse, the integer mass image and the four ancilla-false reversible dilations are one finite case. queue.statement: Write P for the presented inscriptions and O for the internal observations. Supplying <a> after <> changes P from {<>} to {<a>} and leaves O_1 = O_0 = ∅, so no new internal distinction is available. With q : P → N sending an inscription to the distinctions the regime has, x ≠ y in P can hold while q(x) = q(y) in N, so a new presentation does not imply a new internal class, and in the other direction q(x) = q(y) does not imply x = y. Under the opaque convention <a> is a new presentation state in the same internal class as <>; the statement holds under that convention only.
queue.bottleneck: Under the exact-inscription convention <a> is a new state; the statement concerns discriminating power, not meaning, since a regime can gain a syntactic distinction such as empty versus nonempty payload without assigning a a referent. Reviewed in PR 185: lean4/PregenesisPresentationLift.lean checks a two-inscription model (Inscription = {nil, markA}, convention comparison, P0 = {nil} against P1 = {nil, markA}) in which the distinction map q is the constant empty map by definition and the exact-inscription convention is defined as equality, so O_0 = O_1 = empty, the non-injectivity of q and the statement that the collapse holds under the opaque convention only are properties of those definitions. Not proved: an observation family O_n and q derived from it, supplying <a> as an operation that leaves O unchanged, P changing to {<a>} as the statement words it (the model has P1 = {<>, <a>}), the link between q and the Genesis regime model of the module, and the opaque identity convention itself, which stays an import.

queue.statement: Imported inference, audited against Marletto-Vedral (2017, arXiv:1707.06036, pp. 2-3) and Bose et al. (2017, arXiv:1707.06050, pp. 1-2): if two quantum systems Q1 and Q2 start in a separable state, interact only locally through a mediating system M (Q1 <-> M and M <-> Q2, with no direct Q1-Q2 interaction, Principle I locality), and end in an entangled state of Q1 + Q2, then M cannot be a classical medium (in Marletto-Vedral, M must have at least two disjoint incompatible observables whose union is not an information variable; in Bose et al., any mediator modeled by local operations and classical communication cannot create entanglement). The repository has no gravity model; TFQ-0084 is a finite shadow only.
queue.bottleneck: The inference (arXiv:1707.06036 pp. 2-3; arXiv:1707.06050 pp. 1-2) remains an assumption of this branch. ConstructorTheoryMediatorEntanglement.lean states only a finite shadow: a single linear local map A (x) B applied to one pure bipartite state does not raise the rank of its coefficient matrix (any finite dimension over any field), and for two qubits over Q(i) it does not carry the product state (1,1,1,1)/2 to (1,1,1,u)/2 with u=(3+4i)/5, whose squared concurrence is 1/5. Not stated: mixed states, local channels with ancillas, mixtures of branches, classical communication (LOCC), a mediating system M, the definition of a classical medium, or any gravity model.
imported_structure: information-theoretic definition of a classical mediator (assumption)

Collapse and separability are decidable; returned witnesses distinguish, and no witness is equivalent to collapse. queue.statement: Target: on a finite slab lattice the chiral variation of the boundary fermion determinant cancels the bulk Chern-Simons variation. Not established in this checkout. One tested candidate does not realize it, as expected: on open Wilson slabs with U(1) links, the gauge change acts on the Wilson matrix by a diagonal similarity, so the full, interior, boundary Schur and fixed site-matched chiral-block determinants are gauge invariant by construction, while a lifted cup-product CS term whose coefficient is not derived from the fermions changes by 1/32. This is a fixed-basis truncation of a vector-like regulator, not an obstruction to lattice inflow.
queue.bottleneck: Construct a regulated chiral boundary determinant whose projector, basis or measure depends on the gauge field (domain-wall or overlap/Ginsparg-Wilson type), derive from the same fermions the bulk Chern-Simons term they induce, and show that the two gauge variations cancel. The fixed-basis Wilson-slab test cannot register an anomaly, because site-matched fixed bases give similarity-invariant determinants; its bare lifted CS candidate is neither induced by the fermions nor well defined on U(1) links (an integer lift of the same links changes it by 1/8). The continuum Callan-Harvey mechanism remains a literature import.
